---
title: "What does it look like?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

A three-view and the principal dimensions, read back off the `Airplane` object
rather than recomputed from the tables that built it — so this is the geometry
`AeroBuildup` actually sees.

```{python}
wing, stab, fin = mceagle.wings
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-surfaces
#| tbl-cap: "The three flying surfaces. Span and area are the flat pattern — the foam you cut — so the wing's 300 mm is measured along the panel, not tip to tip on the finished glider."
import pandas as pd

pd.DataFrame({
    "surface": [w.name for w in mceagle.wings],
    "span [cm]": [f"{w.span()*100:.1f}" for w in mceagle.wings],
    "root chord [cm]": [f"{w.xsecs[0].chord*100:.2f}" for w in mceagle.wings],
    "area [cm²]": [f"{w.area()*1e4:.1f}" for w in mceagle.wings],
    "aspect ratio": [f"{w.aspect_ratio():.2f}" for w in mceagle.wings],
}).style.hide(axis="index")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-arrangement
#| tbl-cap: "How the three surfaces are arranged on the fuselage."
pd.DataFrame({
    "dimension": [
        "flat pattern span, as cut", "span as built, tips bent up",
        "dihedral", "dihedral tip rise", "fuselage length",
        "tail arm, quarter-chord to quarter-chord",
    ],
    "value": [
        f"{b_w*100:.1f} cm", f"{b_proj*100:.1f} cm", f"{dihedral:.1f}°",
        f"{z_tip*100:.1f} cm", f"{mceagle.fuselages[0].length()*100:.1f} cm",
        f"{(x_qc_h - x_qc_w)*100:.1f} cm",
    ],
}).style.hide(axis="index")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-three-view
#| fig-cap: "The airframe as modelled. The 13.3° dihedral shows in the front view (top right); the stabilizer hangs below the fuselage plate and the fin stands above it, both with their trailing edges at the tail."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 7
# Bind the returned axes -- otherwise their repr renders as a second output and
# demotes the figure to a subfigure.
_ = mceagle.draw_three_view(show=True)
```
